newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas year profit seen slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Qantas year profit seen slightly higher.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd is expected to report on Thursday a slight profit increase for the year to June 1997 due to a soft Japanese market, a competitive local market, but supported by strong U.K. and U.S. markets.

Analysts forecast Qantas, 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, to report a pre-abnormal net profit between A$230 million and A$260 million, with a median forecast of about A$254 million, compared with A$246.2 million in 1995/96.
A fully franked dividend was expected, unchanged at 6.5 cents a share, making a total of 13 cents for the year, and level with the 1995/96 final dividend, aviation analysts said.

"I don't see the dividend changing for next year, which will see the pay-out ratio reduce. It's a high capex (capital expenditure) business, they have the highest dividend yield in the world for an airline," one Sydney-based analyst said.

The profit increase was due mainly to the airline's cost-cutting programme, which has seen the airline chop costs by about A$1.0 billion over the past three years as Qantas faces a revenue slowdown, analysts said.
"I think it will be a good result, the underlining operating costs are important to look at," said another Sydney-based analyst, who forecast a net profit of A$250-A$254 million.
Pru-Bache Securities aviation analyst Andrew Mullholland forecast Qantas to report a pre-abnormal net profit of A$256.5 million for the year.
Ian Myles, aviation analyst at brokers Macquarie Equitiesd estimates the airline will report an annual pre-abnormal net profit of A$253.8 million and a dividend of 6.5 cents per share.
A large abnormal profit was also expected following Qantas' sale of its 19.9 percent stake in Air New Zealand Ltd in March, which produced a profit before tax of A$99 million.
"I think they will use this opportunity to clean-up the balance sheet and so we could see some hefty write-downs," a Melbourne-based analyst said.
Analysts said Qantas may write down the value of its Queensland holiday island business, which have been up for sale for over 12 months for a mooted A$70 million.
The current 1997/98 year is expected to be a better year, with the market estimating double-digit growth to around A$285 million for pre-abnormal net profit, analysts said.

Qantas shares have been one of the strongest industrial stock performers on the local bourse over the past 12 months, rising around 50 percent, compared with the broader market rise of 20 percent during the same time.
Qantas shares closed six cents lower at A$2.97, in line with a big fall in the local stock market following the 3.1 percent slump on Wall Street last Friday.
